# `silk/platform/wasm/host`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Random bytes and clocks from a JavaScript host, for the providers of `Random`, `SystemClock`
and `MonotonicClock` on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

## When to use
Application code does not call it. `OsRandom`, `OsSystemClock` and `OsMonotonicClock` use it
when the program runs in a browser, Node.js, Deno or another JavaScript host, so the same
provider works on every target.

## Details
The module imports two host functions from the import module `silk`, and only a program that
reads random bytes or a clock imports them:

| Import | Does |
|---|---|
| `random(address, length)` | Fills `length` bytes at `address` with secure random bytes, as `crypto.getRandomValues` does |
| `clock(monotonic)` | Returns milliseconds as an `f64`: since 1970 when `monotonic` is 0, since a fixed start (`performance.now()`) when it is 1 |

The standard library's runner, `host/wasm-runner.mjs`, supplies both, and so does the
`mount` of `ui-app-dom`.

## Gotchas
- A host that instantiates the module itself supplies the imports the module names, or the
  instantiation fails.
- A JavaScript host cannot block, so a wait reads the monotonic clock until the deadline. It
  holds the thread, and in a browser page it holds the page.
- A browser rounds `performance.now()`, often to 5 or 100 microseconds.
